text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian foreign minister Algirdas Saudargas arrived on Monday for his first official visit to Latvia and said that there is no territorial dispute between Latvia and Lithuania. Talks on the delimitation of the disputed sea border will be continued on May 23 in Riga.
- Security police found a 200 gram bomb in the sales area of Dressman's store in the centre of Riga after the newspaper Biznes & Baltija received an anonymous phone tip.
- Agriculture minister Roberts Dilba will meet farmers on Saturday to explain the government's agricultural policy.
- Commanders of the armed forces of the three Baltic states continue their working meeting in Riga with military officials from the Nordic countries.
- The faction of the LNNK has picked its candidate for the post of minister of defence and will name him later today.
- Minister of Communications Vilis Krishtopans announced plans for restructuring Latvia's Railway Company.
- Agrosin Pte, the new owner of the Liepaja metallurgical plant, is going to invest $5.5 million in the modernization of the plant's rolling shop.
